title: Higher compact-support base change along a locally closed immersion
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. For every separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $S_0$ write $S=S_0\times_{k_0}k$. Use the common-stage coefficient categories $D^b_c(S,\Qlb)$, their constructible hearts and their Weil objects as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex; def-weil-constructible-heart]. A Weil complex is a pair with a geometric-Frobenius isomorphism; no triangulated structure on the category of pairs is assumed. Write $Rf_{0!}$ for the compact-support functor of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], with its induced Weil structure, and $\mathcal H^r$ for the standard heart-valued cohomology functors [prop-constructible-truncations].

Let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}X'_0&\xrightarrow{g_0}&X_0\\ f'_0\downarrow&&\downarrow f_0\\ Y'_0&\xrightarrow{h_0}&Y_0\end{array}$$
be Cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with all four schemes separated of finite type over $k_0$, $f_0$ separated of finite type, and $h_0$ a locally closed immersion (a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion; def-weil-open-immersion]). All pullbacks are the derived coefficient pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; on constructible hearts their notation means their exact restriction. For every constructible Weil complex $K$ on $X_0$ and every $r\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical compact-support base-change map induces a natural isomorphism of constructible Weil sheaves
$$h_0^*\mathcal H^r(Rf_{0!}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^r(Rf'_{0!}g_0^*K).$$
For a constructible Weil sheaf $F$ on $X_0$, this specializes to
$$h_0^*R^rf_{0!}F\xrightarrow{\sim}R^rf'_{0!}(g_0^*F),\qquad R^rf_{0!}F:=\mathcal H^r(Rf_{0!}(F[0])).$$
Both isomorphisms are induced by $\mathcal H^r$ of the canonical derived exchange $h_0^*Rf_{0!}\to Rf'_{0!}g_0^*$, using the standard cohomology comparisons for immersion pullbacks. They intertwine the Weil structures and are natural in $K$, respectively $F$. No properness of $f_0$ or smoothness of $h_0$ is assumed.

proof.text: Base change the given Cartesian square from $k_0$ to $k$, and forget the Weil structures temporarily. Apply clause (4) of [prop-functor-package] at the common-stage $\Qlb$ coefficient stage to the underlying object of $K$. Its hypotheses are exactly the separated finite-type scheme setting and separated finite-type $f_0$ assumed here; the compact-support clause permits arbitrary base change, so applies to $h_0$ without properness or smoothness. It gives the actual canonical exchange isomorphism $B_K:h_0^*Rf_{0!}K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf\prime_{0!}g_0^*K$. By clause (1) of [fix-lem-exchanges], this is the specified compact-support exchange, natural in the coefficient object. The field-coefficient assertion of [fix-prop-coherence] says that these comparison maps are Weil-equivariant. Thus $B_K$ is an isomorphism of Weil pairs, natural in $K$; no triangulated structure on the category of pairs is used.

proof.text: Put $L=Rf_{0!}K$, which is bounded constructible by the domain assertion in [prop-functor-package]. Clause (1) of [lem-zl-immersion-weil-local-behavior], applied to the locally closed immersion $h_0$, supplies the canonical natural Weil isomorphism $c_{h,L}^r:\mathcal H^r(h_0^*L)\xrightarrow{\sim}h_0^*\mathcal H^r(L)$ for every $r\in\mathbf Z$. In particular this comparison uses the standard constructible heart, with the same common-stage coefficients as $B_K$.

source.place: Part 2: taking cohomology through the two immersion pullbacks in the compact-support base-change isomorphisms (old steps 7 and 9).

proof.text: Apply the heart-valued cohomology functor of [prop-constructible-truncations] to $B_K$. The required arrow is explicitly $\mathcal H^r(B_K)\circ(c_{h,L}^r)^{-1}$. It is invertible: its inverse is $c_{h,L}^r\circ\mathcal H^r(B_K^{-1})$, by the identity and composition laws of a functor. Both factors are natural and Weil-equivariant by the preceding steps, so their composite is as well. This proves the complex assertion, with precisely the required canonical map and without a choice of a different exchange.

source.place: Part 2: taking cohomology through the two immersion pullbacks in the compact-support base-change isomorphisms (old steps 7 and 9).

proof.text: For a constructible Weil sheaf $F$, take $K=F[0]$. By [lem-a1-constructible-pullback-t-exact] applied to the geometric map $g:X\prime\to X$, $g^*$ restricts to the exact functor of constructible hearts, hence the canonical heart embedding identifies $g_0^*(F[0])$ with $(g_0^*F)[0]$. This identification is the pullback comparison on heart objects and is Weil-equivariant by the field-coefficient coherence of [fix-prop-coherence]. Substitution in the arrow of step 3 gives $h_0^*R^rf_{0!}F\xrightarrow{\sim}R^rf\prime_{0!}(g_0^*F)$, since $R^r(-)_!$ in the statement is defined by $\mathcal H^r$ on the degree-zero input. Naturality follows by substituting the degree-zero image of every morphism $F\to F\prime$ into the naturality square in step 3.
